question: Does the sample market spend the budget better than uniform allocation and plain successive halving? (PLAN 8, PLAN 9 E5)

shared_run_settings.comment: identical for every arm; arms differ only in allocation. Every arm gets the same contrarian proposals, so the candidate pools match; wallets start fresh in each cell (memory is per cell), so seeds are independent. No screening target: config has none, so halving/market screen on the dev target and merge those samples
shared_run_settings.models: dev roles from configs/models.json (python3 -m autoresearch.research.models_config 'dev flags'); the data files are gitignored and regenerated by scripts/convert_evalawarebench.py --fetch

primary_metric.name: $ per validated finding
primary_metric.how: per run: report.compute.cost_usd (API calls at list price plus the dev target's GPU time) / number of findings with status 'validated' (runs with none count as no finding at that cost); per arm: ratio of totals over seeds with a bootstrap 90% CI over seeds

secondary_metrics: anytime curve: best dev score against cumulative $ (report.anytime), mean over seeds per arm, with the score at fixed $ = 5, 10, 15
$ and wall time to the first validated finding (report.anytime)
held-out score of the final design (evaluate-design --mode final, as in E4)
market only: final wallets and mean log score per agent, Brier score of bids (report.market)
samples spent per round and screened-out candidates (report.allocation)
analysis: per arm: mean and bootstrap 90% CI over the 8 seeds; P(market < uniform) on $ per validated finding by bootstrap over seeds; plots from scripts/plots.py (anytime curve, market vs uniform vs halving)
success_criteria: market <= uniform in $ per validated finding (PLAN 9 E5)
market's held-out score is not below uniform's 90% CI (the market must not buy cheapness with worse designs)
all arms reported, including a null or a market that loses
estimated_cost: capped at $15 per run by --max-cost, API list price plus the target's GPU time (24 runs, at most $360); GPU idle time before scale-to-zero is extra and must be read off the Modal bill; to firm up after one cheap live seed per arm
reporting: seeds, sample counts, CODE_VERSION per cell, failed and negative results all reported; offline-simulator numbers never presented as real-model numbers
heldout_evaluation: python3 scripts/batch_final.py results/e5 --llm anthropic-batch --yes -- --benchmark-items data/benchmarks/evalawarebench_original.jsonl --probe-questions data/benchmarks/evaldetect_probes.json --samples 3, once per held-out target in configs/models.json 'final flags' (--heldout-target / --heldout-judges as printed there); Sonnet 4.5 retires 2026-11-30, so its held-out pass must run before then

environment.OPENAI_COMPAT_USD_PER_HOUR: 3.95 (one Modal H100 at list price; check modal.com/pricing at launch and record the value used). OpenAICompatLLM charges the target's busy GPU time to Budget at this rate (llm.GpuMeter, a lower bound: idle-before-scale-to-zero and cold starts are not seen), so --max-cost and $ per validated finding include the target
environment.OPENAI_COMPAT_PLAIN_THINKING: as set for the C1 calibration gate (the probe calls must match the calibrated setting)
